messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test failure is related to parsing octal values in tar header fields, specifically in username and groupname fields that might be NUL or empty. From the bug report, version 1.8 no longer decompresses tar files with entries having null or empty usernames or group names, causing an IOException "Error detected parsing the header".

The key method under scrutiny is TarUtils.parseOctal(). It parses a byte array representing an octal number, trimming leading spaces and trailing NUL (0) and space characters before conversion. This method is used in TarArchiveEntry.parseTarHeader() to parse numeric fields (userId, groupId, sizes, etc.) from the header.

TarArchiveEntry.parseTarHeader(byte[],ZipEncoding,boolean) extracts fields from the tar header including userName and groupName strings via TarUtils.parseName(). This method returns an empty string if the entire name field consists of NUL bytes.

If the username or groupname is NUL bytes, parseName returns an empty string, but the numeric userId, groupId fields are still parsed via parseOctalOrBinary, which internally uses parseOctal(). If the fields contain unexpected NUL values, parseOctal may throw IllegalArgumentException.

In TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry(), when a TarArchiveEntry is constructed from the header bytes, it calls parseTarHeader, and if IllegalArgumentException occurs (e.g. from parseOctal due to invalid input region), it is wrapped as an IOException with message "Error detected parsing the header".

The reported regression likely stems from more strict or different parsing behaviors in parseOctal or related code. In particular, parseOctal throws if trimmed data becomes empty after stripping spaces/NUL or if invalid octal characters appear. Previously, such fields may have been tolerated as zero or empty. This strictness breaks valid decompression of older archives that use all NUL for username/groupname.

The testParseOctal unit test shows typical input cases for parseOctal including trimming spaces and NUL ending bytes, but it does not cover empty or all-NUL fields as usernames.

In summary, the root cause is the stricter handling in parseOctal (called during TarArchiveEntry header parsing) that errors on all-NUL or empty fields in username or groupname bytes in tar headers, leading to decomposition failure flagged by IOException from TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry().

To fix, parseOctal or the header parsing logic must tolerate empty and NUL-only fields for username/groupname gracefully instead of throwing, matching previous behavior.

This diagnosis leverages analysis of:
- The failing test calling TarUtils.parseOctal() on various inputs.
- The bug report describing failure decompressing archives with NUL username/group.
- TarUtils.parseOctal() source code showing strict validation.
- TarArchiveEntry.parseTarHeader() decoding header fields using parseOctal and parseName.
- TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry() wrapping IllegalArgumentException from header parsing as IOException.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
